reuse.why: Every weekend/holiday decision (move, skip for daily, holiday match including MM-DD) is folded into the existing getDateWithSkippedWeekend, which getNextDate, getUpcomingDates, the new getDatesInRange and schedule-template all call; lookahead bounds come from shared helpers.

duplication.why: No logic is copied, but each caller still writes its own 'skipWeekend ? getDateWithSkippedWeekend(...) : date' wrapper and both getNextDate and getUpcomingDates decide 'daily with weekend handling' themselves to size the lookahead.

placement.why: The rule, the holiday predicate and the shift/lookahead bounds live in shared/schedules.ts; server handlers and the budget template only consume them.

scope.why: Changes cover the four steps (daily skip, range handler, holidays, recurring holidays) and their tests, with no unrelated edits.

maintainability.why: One function owns the weekend/holiday policy and signals a skipped daily occurrence with null, which keeps rule changes in one place; the null contract makes the schedule-template loop condition harder to read.

bypasses_abstraction.where: none; all date sites go through getDateWithSkippedWeekend

disguised_duplication.where: none; the repeated skipWeekend ternary is the same call wrapper the tree already had, not reshaped logic

abstraction_drift.where: getDateWithSkippedWeekend gained frequency and holidays parameters and a 'daily -> null' branch, which is how the requested rule is centralised; no call site re-implements it, though getNextDate and getUpcomingDates each compute their own daily flag for the lookahead size.
